chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Fadala ibn Ayyub from Aban from Abdullah ibn Sinan said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who makes a gift (hiba), does he return it if he wishes or not? He said: 'The gift is valid for those of kinship and the one who is rewarded for his gift, and he returns in other cases if he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: Can a person revoke a gift they gave to their relatives in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while gifts to non-relatives are generally revocable at the donor's will, those given to close relatives (dhawi al-qurba) are binding to encourage kinship ties, unless the donor explicitly intends to earn reward (thawab) or derives specific benefit. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on 'silat al-qurba' (maintaining family bonds) as a spiritual obligation that restricts the donor's right of revocation, distinguishing it from mere commercial transactions.
